summary: Monaco’s two high-relevance pledges are urban measures combining restoration and conservation. Its renaturation plan seeks to transform at least 20% of the road surfaces, themselves reported as approximately 30% of Monaco’s area, into biodiversity-friendly space by 2030, representing a gain of more than 13 ha. The tree programme aims for at least a 20% increase in urban tree numbers by 2030, equivalent to 2,400 additional trees alongside 12,000 already present. Both commitments therefore concentrate on nature-positive management within a very compact urban territory rather than agricultural restoration. The supplied geography lists only settlement cover, at 3 km², but also gives a 2 km² total land area; the resulting 155.6% share is internally inconsistent, while still indicating that these are city-scale interventions.

targets.context: At least 20% of road surfaces reported as approximately 30% of Monaco; the stated gain of more than 13 ha exceeds 6.5% of the reported 2 km² total land area.
The stated increase equates to planting 2,400 additional trees, alongside the 12,000 trees already present.
